solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Breaking into bundle of notes, set off to get very drunk

indicators.note: something breaking into a bundle forces its way inside it, so the jumbled letters go within the bundle

parts.note: a wad is a thick roll of banknotes

indicators.note: set off can mean spoilt or gone wrong, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone splits open a roll of cash and sets off on a heavy drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as 'departed', but 'off' signals that the letters of 'set' are jumbled. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, as in being wrecked or plastered after a night out.

clue.text: Bustle previously spring- loaded?

indicators.note: the spring comes previously, before the bustle

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A bustle, the dress pad, worn with a spring inside it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring-loaded' reads as mechanical; split it, and 'loaded' is slang for rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for wealthy, and so is comfortably off or affluent.

clue.text: Great 11, perhaps, for what 1 down might pay

parts.note: super means great
11 down is a vote of thanks; reading it as thanks plus a vote gives TA (thanks) and X (a vote cast with a cross)

explanation.surface: A grand expression of gratitude in exchange for what the rich are charged.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; X marks a vote on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional levy on high incomes, the kind wealthy people would be charged.

clue.text: Dress up as an archbishop

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: Putting on vestments to play the part of a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. Archbishops of York sign themselves EBOR, from the Latin Eboracum.
explanation.definitionFit: The official signature of the Archbishop of York, abbreviated from the Latin name of the city.

clue.text: Saint Christopher? Sporting this, when nervous and easily scared

parts.note: Kit is a familiar short form of the name Christopher

indicators.note: sporting can mean frolicking or playing about, so the letters of this are jumbled

explanation.surface: A saint's medal worn by a jumpy traveller seeking reassurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like 'wearing'; here it signals an anagram of THIS, giving TISH. 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a horse or person that is jumpy, skittery and prone to take fright.

clue.text: Surfing before getting on plane

indicators.note: the plane's word comes before the word for getting on

parts.note: kite is old RAF slang for an aircraft
boarding is getting on a vehicle

explanation.surface: A surfer heads out to the waves just before catching a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'getting on plane' as 'boarding a kite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A water sport, surfing while towed by a large hand-held kite.

clue.text: Printing machine of sort used by Wanderer?

parts.note: type means sort or kind
Wanderer is this puzzle's setter, the crossword compiler

explanation.surface: A query about what kind of printing press a traveller uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanderer' looks like a traveller; it is this puzzle's setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that sets type for printing, composing text before it is printed.

clue.text: Treated nail — one with diamonds embedded

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of nail are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A manicured nail set with a single diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Set into a surface so as to be flush with it, like mother-of-pearl in a box lid.

clue.text: Drawing a veil over bad defeat

definitions.meaning: concealing or keeping something out of sight
a thrashing, a heavy beating in a game

explanation.surface: Covering up a humiliating loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both concealing something and a thrashing, as in taking a hiding at football.

clue.text: PC Plod's tip: suspect a plot at first

indicators.note: says the jumbled letters come first, with the single letter after them
suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters of a plot are rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter, here the start of Plod

explanation.surface: A bumbling policeman's advice: suspect a conspiracy before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: PC Plod is a comic British nickname for a policeman; but 'PC' is the definition, personal computer. LAPTO comes first, then P.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal computer is one example of a PC, small enough to rest on your knees.

clue.text: After small drink, daughter did something dotty

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is placed after the small drink

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: After a nip of something, a daughter behaves a little crazily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' looks like 'crazy'; it means 'made with dots'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to apply paint or engrave in small dots, literally a dotted technique.

clue.text: Formal show of appreciation, given actor playing R Langdon's cross?

parts.note: a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper
Tom Hanks played Robert Langdon in the Dan Brown films; 'T Hanks's' read as 'of T Hanks'

explanation.surface: A formal thank-you given to the actor who played Robert Langdon.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Langdon is the hero of The Da Vinci Code; 'cross' means an X, the mark of a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or motion expressing gratitude, typically at the end of a meeting.

clue.text: Sailor paid upfront for protective cover

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: upfront points to the very front letter of the word paid

explanation.surface: A sailor pays in advance to cover himself for risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for tarpaulin, a waterproof sheet used to shield things from the weather.

clue.text: Burning bush initially featured in Milton work? Wrong — in OT!

indicators.note: the letter is featured inside the title of the Milton work

parts.note: Comus is a masque by John Milton

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of bush
wrong signals that the letters of in OT are put out of order

explanation.surface: A query whether the burning bush appears in Milton, corrected: it is in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The burning bush appears in Exodus, in the Old Testament; Milton's masque is the 'work'. 'Wrong' signals the anagram of 'in OT'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical process of burning, fuel reacting with oxygen to give heat and flame.

clue.text: N American state capital: third of visits for man's best friends

parts.note: Chihuahua is both a Mexican state and its capital city

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of the word visits

explanation.surface: A trip to a Mexican state capital for some dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. Mexico is in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are called man's best friend, and these are a breed of tiny dog.

clue.text: End with what might be a fine sentence

parts.note: death is the end of life
a fine is one kind of penalty

explanation.surface: A neat closing line that could be a well-turned sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine sentence' reads as a nicely crafted phrase; 'sentence' is a court's judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital punishment is a sentence handed down by a court for the gravest crimes.

clue.text: Capsize public vessel

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
an urn is a vessel or container

explanation.surface: A ferry, a public vessel, turning over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a boat, fitting 'Capsize'; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn upside down, the way a boat flips over in rough water.

clue.text: Dine with mate suffering form of insanity

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters of dine and mate are disturbed

explanation.surface: Eating with a friend who has a mental illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic decline in memory and reasoning, a condition of mental deterioration.

clue.text: Masterpieces from cooks badly overdue

parts.note: chefs are cooks

indicators.note: badly says the letters of overdue are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Fine dishes from cooks who are very late serving them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word. The French phrase means 'masterworks'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English for an artist's finest works, literally 'master works'.

clue.text: One-dimensional storyteller touring Geordieland

indicators.note: the storyteller tours, going around, the region

parts.note: one who tells stories is a liar
Geordies come from Newcastle in north-east England, NE

explanation.surface: A shallow novelist on a book tour in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-dimensional' looks like an insult for the storyteller; it is the definition, meaning 'in a line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying along a single line, having only length, as in mathematics.

clue.text: Problem sleeping? One surprisingly found in alpha male relative

parts.note: A is alpha in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are found inside the word for a male relative

parts.note: pa is a father

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of one come out unexpectedly arranged

explanation.surface: An alpha male's relative has a sleeping disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha male' reads as a dominant man, but alpha is just its letter and the male relative is a father. 'surprisingly' scrambles 'One'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical condition in which breathing stops briefly during sleep, often with snoring.

clue.text: One politician with base longing for what some think Trump needs?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
e is the base of natural logarithms
aching means yearning

explanation.surface: A low-minded politician craves what some believe the US president deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like 'low'; it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Formally charging a president with misconduct, the process some critics wanted for Donald Trump.

clue.text: Somewhat poor female swimmer

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather weak woman at the swimming baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish, the ide, often kept in ornamental ponds; fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: Cake, good for a bribe

parts.note: a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: Offering a cake to someone as a sweetener.
explanation.walkthrough: British slang for a backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an illicit payment to secure a favour, a backhander.

clue.text: The Spanish books cover heartless ruler that's fluently persuasive

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: the books' letters cover, or go around, the shortened ruler

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word for ruler

parts.note: a queen is a ruler

explanation.surface: Spanish books about a cruel monarch who could talk anyone round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central letter of the ruler, and 'cover' puts the books around what is left. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with fluency and power to move people is what being articulate and expressive means.

clue.text: Upheaval in corporation last month

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Turmoil at a company during the previous month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company; it is jokey slang for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is uproar and commotion, a violent disturbance.

clue.text: Have another look at animals kept in reserve briefly

indicators.note: the animals are kept inside the shortened reserve

parts.note: res is a short form of reserve
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: Checking again on animals housed in a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate again is to take a second look and judge anew.

clue.text: Characteristic content of sugar in African country

definitions.text: Characteristic content of sugar in African country

parts.words: Characteristic content of sugar in African country
parts.note: the inner characters of sugar, listed one by one with a conjunction before the last, spell out the country's name

explanation.surface: The typical make-up of sugar grown in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characteristic' means 'about the characters': strip the S and R from sugar and describe the three letters left in words, joining the last two with 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked East African republic whose capital is Kampala.
